text.tspan: The kernel runs on one identity map (virtual == physical, supervisor-only).
Every LibOS gets its own page tables, confined to a window above 64 TiB. Not to scale.
only if the caller owns paddr
Why 64 TiB: the kernel map is identity,
so a lower window would overlap
above RAM, in the PCI MMIO hole
4 KiB pages, each tagged with an owner
kernel: page tables, heap, mixer rings
per LibOS: PML4 + tables, code, data, stack,
holds the PMM bitmap and the owner table
.bss holds the 24 KiB boot page tables,
the 16 KiB boot stack, the 16 KiB syscall stack
Below 64 TiB: PML4 slot 0, shared by every
identity map. Ring 3 reaches none of it.
